newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom office bombed in Corsica.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom office bombed in Corsica.

text.p: A bomb blew up outside offices of state-owned France Telecom overnight in Bastia, northern Corsica, smashing windows and damaging the building but causing no injuries, police said on Thursday.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast but such bombings are a common tactic of Corsican separatist guerrillas seeking greater autonomy from mainland France for the Mediterranean island.
A second overnight blast damaged a carpenter's car in Bonifacio, southern Corsica, police added.

One of 15 individuals rounded up in a police swoop on Corsica on Monday has been formally placed under investigation and remanded in custody in an Ajaccio prison on suspicion of criminal conspiracy, reviving a banned organisation and destruction of goods and property with explosives, police added.
Patrick Tesi, 41, was believed to be an activist member of the banned hardline separatist Historic Wing of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), police said.
Monday's roundup had been aimed at finding those responsible for a recent spate of bombings on Corsica.
FLNC separatists have claimed hundreds of bombings in their two-decade-long separatist campaign.
Recent targets have included tax and post offices, bank branches and offices of state-run companies France-Telecom and Air France.
